record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: Let p* be the minimal size of a centered family of infinite subsets of N that is not linearly refinable modulo finite sets. Is p equal to p*?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in ZFC. Let ω denote the natural numbers, and for A,B ⊆ ω write A ⊆* B (A is almost contained in B) when A \ B is finite. A family F ⊆ [ω]^ω of infinite subsets of ω is called centered if every finite subfamily has infinite intersection. A pseudo-intersection of F is an infinite set A ⊆ ω with A ⊆* B for every B ∈ F. A family L ⊆ [ω]^ω is said to linearly refine F (modulo finite) if L is linearly ordered by ⊆*, and for every B ∈ F there exists A ∈ L with A ⊆* B.

Define:
 • p = the minimal cardinality of a centered family F ⊆ [ω]^ω which has no pseudo-intersection (the pseudo-intersection number);
 • p* = the minimal cardinality of a centered family F ⊆ [ω]^ω which is not linearly refinable modulo finite, i.e. admits no linearly (⊆*-) ordered refining family.

Decide whether p = p* is provable in ZFC.
artifact.status_search_result: The cardinal p* was renamed lr (the linear refinement number). Machura, Shelah and Tsaban (Fundamenta Mathematicae, "The linear refinement number and selection theory", 2014) proved that it is consistent that p < lr < c, and in particular that p < p*. Hence p = p* is not a theorem of ZFC; the question is resolved in the negative.

status_evidence.title: The linear refinement number and selection theory
status_evidence.snippet: The linear refinement number lr is the minimal cardinality of a centered family in [ω]^ω such that no linearly (⊆*-)ordered family refines it. ... Consistently, p < lr.
status_evidence.claim: Consistency of p < lr (= p*) is established, refuting ZFC-provability of p = p*.

status_evidence.title: The linear refinement number and selection theory (Shelah archive)
status_evidence.snippet: lr had previously been denoted p*; we prove the consistency of p < lr.
status_evidence.claim: p* (=lr) is consistently strictly larger than p.
